## TL;DR

Close-out progress no longer sits in the task drawer's action row. While Move to done is running, `integrating · <step> · <elapsed>` is the full-width status line under the preview row, using the same status card as a live coding run. The action row keeps the state dropdown, the D/R chip, Stop work, and Stop MTD. Move to done returns only after the task leaves the pipeline, so a changing timer cannot wrap Stop MTD onto a second line.

## Work and rationale

The variable-width control was the Move to done button. When `inPipeline` was true its label became `integrationCardLabel` (the same string the board card shows) and the button was disabled. That string includes the current step and a live elapsed time, so the button grew and shrank. It used the real button style, so it looked clickable and did nothing. Stop MTD, the control that actually cancels the job, was pushed down with the preview row.

The status region under the preview row already had one card, `drawer-status-summary`, chosen by `selectDrawerStatus`. A coding task renders `coding · active …` there. Close-out never entered that function, so the only place the step appeared was the disabled button. During a check run the heading helper could already return the integration label, but building a candidate or running remote tests often has no local check run, so the card stayed empty and the button carried the text.

`integrating` is now a candidate in `selectDrawerStatus`, after exhausted checks and before routine check, handoff, reviewer, and work progress. One key still wins. A higher card (needs input, review failed, not landable, handoff failed, checks failed) keeps the slot. The integration line is appended to that card's lines when it is not already there, so close-out does not add a second element. When close-out is the winner, the card is one running line: the shared integration label, with the same activity indicator treatment as other live statuses. It stays a status card that opens Debug → Status details. It is not an action-row button, so it has no status-button fill.

The Move to done button is omitted while the task is in the pipeline. Stop MTD stays. When the job ends, Move to done comes back with the stable label, not the step text. Header chips skip `integrating`, matching other live statuses that already have the card.

Shot fixtures `drawer:closeOutBuilding` and `drawer:closeOutRemoteTests`, plus narrow variants at 360px, seed review task `#9999` with a heartbeating pipeline on "building candidate" or "remote tests". Declared shots point at `/work?task=9999` and highlight `.drawer-status-summary`. `user-docs/review-and-close-out.md` now describes the status-line placement and the action row. The fixture list in `docs/previews.md` and the example list in `user-docs/running-with-agents.md` include the new drawer states.

## Approaches tried

Leaving Move to done visible but pinning its label to "Move to done" while disabled was the smaller edit. It still left a control that looks clickable and does nothing, which the spec rules out. The action row is specified as real controls only: dropdown, D/R chip, Stop work, Stop MTD.

A second status node beside a higher-priority card would have broken the one-card rule from #0952. Folding the line into the selected card keeps a single `.drawer-status-summary`. Ranking close-out above generic "checks running" matters because a pipeline job's own label already names the step; a second "Checks running" card would duplicate it.

Reusing `drawer-status-summary` avoided new CSS. The card already has the full-width layout, theme tokens, and contrast treatment used for `coding · active`. A bespoke pill would have failed the "match the existing status line" criterion and the hard-coded-color guard.

## Challenges and blockers

The integration label is shared with the board card (`integrationActiveCopy` plus `integrationProgressCardLabel`). The drawer must keep that string so the panel and the card stay in agreement (#1023). The new card reads that computed label; it does not format a second clock.

`selectDrawerStatus` is a pure priority list. The fold of the close-out line into a higher card lives in the drawer, because the function returns one key, not a composite. The unit test covers the close-out case: integrating alone, integrating over checks and work, and a blocking card over integrating. A component test checks that a review-failed card still renders once and contains both "Review failed" and the integration label, and that the action row does not.

Shot declaration goes through `repoos update`, which writes the live board copy. Handoff reads that canonical body for `## Shots`, so the worktree copy of the task file lagging is expected.

## Key learnings

The action row and the status card are different jobs. Live prose that changes length belongs in the status card, which is full width and already budgeted as one element. Putting it in a button couples layout to a timer.

Close-out is a status, not a check-run alias. Stages such as building a candidate have no `activeCheckRun`, so hooking the label only to "checks running" misses the bug in the screenshots. A dedicated priority key makes those stages show up, and still yields when a human-facing card is more important.
